answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a meaningful deposit in a public registry before it can trade. A hollow identity with no stake earns nothing, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand deposits, a cost that scales with the attack and is charged at the dawn of every epoch. Reputation then accrues transparently, like a crystal record of past work, so honest agents grow more trusted while fresh sybils stay untrusted and unprofitable.
